identification.summary: OnionDog is a name given by Qihoo 360's Helios Team (SkyEye Labs) in 2016 to an activity cluster that reportedly stole data from energy and transportation organizations in Korean-speaking countries, with activity traced back to October 2013 [S2]. In August 2017 Trend Micro assessed that OnionDog is not a targeted attack but a cyber drill, because several of the eight C&C IP addresses in the 360 report were linked to South Korea's National Cybersecurity Center (NCSC) [S1][S3].
identification.firstObserved: 360 Helios: activity traced back to October 2013 [S2].
identification.notes: The existing record's country value (KP) is not supported by any source gathered here; neither the 360 report coverage nor Trend Micro attributes OnionDog to North Korea [S1][S2]. The two vendor readings conflict (real APT per 360, drill per Trend Micro) and this record does not resolve them [S1][S2].

attribution.basis: No source gathered names a sponsor. 360 Helios described a group but the coverage reviewed names no state [S2]. Trend Micro, reviewing the same indicators, assessed the samples were linked to official South Korean cyber practices (the NCSC) and concluded this was a cyber drill, not a targeted attack [S1][S3].

sectors: Transportation (harbors, vessel traffic services, subways, public transportation)
targeting.notes: 360 Helios reported 2014 targeting of electric power and water resources corporations and other energy enterprises, and 2015 targeting of harbors, VTS, subways and public transportation [S2]. The existing record also lists government as a target; no source gathered here confirms this. All targeting claims derive from the 360 report and are disputed by Trend Micro [S1].

capabilities.summary: 360 Helios reported spear-phishing email lures, an early Trojan disguised as a Hangul (HWP) document using icons and file numbers, later use of a vulnerability in an upgraded Hangul version to embed malicious code in a genuine HWP file, and a USB worm to reach network-isolated targets [S2]. Helios reported 96 groups of malicious code and 14 C&C domains/IPs [S2]. Trend Micro reviewed the eight hardcoded C&C IPs and said the malware does no actual harm to systems and that about 200 unique samples are known [S1][S3].

campaigns.name: 360 Helios publishes OnionDog report
campaigns.summary: The Helios Team at 360 SkyEye Labs disclosed OnionDog with IoCs including file hashes and eight C&C IPs [S2].

campaigns.name: Trend Micro reassessment: cyber drill
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro used historic passive DNS to link several of the eight C&C IPs to South Korea's NCSC (ncsc.go.kr hostnames, historic resolutions 2011-2013) and concluded OnionDog is a cyber drill, not a targeted attack [S1][S3].

diamond.adversary: Unknown. 360 described a group; Trend Micro assessed official South Korean (NCSC) cyber-practice activity [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Spear-phishing, malicious/fake HWP documents, Hangul vulnerability, USB worm for isolated networks [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Eight hardcoded C&C IPs, several linked by Trend Micro to NCSC-associated domains [S1]; 14 C&C domains/IPs per Helios [S2].
diamond.victim: Energy and transportation organizations in Korean-speaking countries per 360 [S2]; Trend Micro disputes that these were real victims [S1].
diamond.technology: Reliance on Hangul word-processor documents in Korean organizations, and USB media crossing isolated networks [S2].

gaps: Core dispute: 360 presented a real APT; Trend Micro concluded a cyber drill. Neither is independently confirmed by the South Korean government in the sources gathered [S1][S2].

No sponsor or state attribution is stated in any source gathered; the KP country value in the original record is unsupported. A secondary vendor blog reportedly links OnionDog to Lazarus, but this was not verified and Qianxin's own report reportedly says no link was found; not used here.
The original 360/Qianxin report and Trend Micro appendix (hashes) could not be opened (WebFetch failed); details rely on search summaries and secondary coverage.
No aliases or MITRE group are established. Help Net Security, ETDA, Malpedia and CFR pages were not opened.
Actor objectives and any post-2017 activity are not documented in sources gathered.
